interest: Herbert Houston's plan for reciprocal information libraries.
overview: Decimal file 894.428 (Education: Libraries - Japan) primarily documents an August–September 1934 initiative by American publisher and civic organizer Herbert S. Houston to establish a network of international information libraries, beginning with a reciprocal United States Library of Information in Tokyo and a Japanese Library of Information in New York modeled after the British Library of Information. Writing to Secretary of State Cordell Hull and Acting Secretary William Phillips, Houston describes his previous discussions with Japanese leaders, including Viscount Ishii, Baron Dan, Prince Tokugawa, and Prince Konoye, and argues that institutionalized cultural information centers could dispel international misunderstandings and war clouds. While the State Department expresses sympathy and forwards the concept to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo, it notes the unavailability of government funds and emphasizes private sponsorship. The exchange culminates in Houston's announcement that the Japanese Foreign Office approved funding for a New York library and invited the World Federation of Education Associations to Tokyo for 1935. The file also contains an appended 1938 transmittal letter from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Librarian of Congress Herbert Putnam enclosing an Embassy Peiping despatch on the historic Pei T'ang Cathedral Library in China.

subfiles.about: Herbert S. Houston proposes to Secretary of State Cordell Hull the establishment of a United States Library of Information in Tokyo and reciprocal institutions in other major capitals.

subfiles.about: The Department of State responds to Houston's proposal, stating that no government funds are available but offering unofficial encouragement and referring the matter to Ambassador Grew.
subfiles.summary: Phillips says no funds exist but welcomes Houston's library idea.
subfiles.title: Letter from Acting Secretary William Phillips to Herbert S. Houston on Information Libraries

subfiles.about: Instruction No. 584 transmitting Houston's proposal and the Department's reply to Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo for comments.

subfiles.about: Herbert S. Houston expresses appreciation for the referral to Ambassador Grew and confidentially mentions plans for a German Library of Information.

subfiles.about: Houston notifies Phillips that the Japanese Foreign Office has approved funds for a Japanese Library of Information in New York and invited an educational convention to Tokyo.

subfiles.about: Acting Secretary Phillips welcomes news of the Japanese Library of Information in New York and endorses the concept of a reciprocal American library in Tokyo.
